correctness.rationale: The binary two-gram count class for a linear word is determined by transition loops a=N00,b=N11 and cross counts c=N01,d=N10. Feasibility forces |c-d|<=1. For c=d=j>=1, two endpoint orientations yield B_j(a,b)=(m/j) C(a+j-1,j-1)C(b+j-1,j-1), a+b=m-2j. For |c-d|=1, only one endpoint orientation gives U_j=binomial product. Strict log-concavity balances a,b when j>=2; for j=1 all loop allocations tie. The ratio B_{j+1}*/B_j* identifies k=ceil(m/4) and exceptional adjacent tie when m=1 mod4; direct inequality B_{j0}*>max U excludes all imbalanced transitions. Central-binomial Stirling yields F_n~2^(n+1)/(pi(n-1)). Independent direct enumeration of 131,064 binary words n=3..16 checked 1,078 profile classes and every equality profile. The all-length proof is analytic.
